data.body:
Phase 1 classification on current origin/main 89128b2e09 — design conflict, no automatic repair.

Proven mechanism: adding the exact [operator-attested] marker to a criterion after plan certification edits description material, so material_diff invalidates the signed attestation as stale-material before completion verification can reuse it. A fresh direct runtime reproduction changed material ea05cf9eb7de02ec to 10d590f34a282dab and changed CLOSE validity from certified to stale-material. A control with the marker present before certification, followed only by a concrete evidence comment, kept material b90899f7acdb0b91 and CLOSE validity certified. Focused lifecycle controls passed, and the recent origin/main fixes did not touch the relevant gate files.

Legitimacy: the stale-material result is intended anti-tamper behavior from the original plan-review material-pinning design; silently exempting a late description edit would weaken that contract. The conflicting artifact is completion-verifier remediation guidance that requires a material description edit after delivery. This is therefore a design conflict, not an unintended implementation defect that rebar-debug may auto-repair.

Decision required: choose a durable operator-attestation design. Options include requiring criteria to be marked before plan review, representing late operator evidence in a signed non-material event rather than description text, or explicitly authorizing a narrowly-scoped post-review material transformation with its own attestation semantics. No code or ticket status change was made.
